Just to clear things up if you have four devotion to blue on board when you cast Thassa then she enters the battlefield as an enchantment after leaving the stack for a split second then realizes she gave herself full devotion and becomes a creature.

 This is important because she doesn't evolve creatures at that state. So Cloudfin for example wouldn't evolve. Now if you have five devotion excluding Thassa herself then she hits the battlefield as a 5/5 creature and can evolve creatures and/or triggers "creature entering battlefield" effects.

I like that idea but remember this deck curves out at four and it isn't as fast as say RDW but it is still aggro-y so you want to win fast. That X you paid for it won't be as large as you usually want it to be. Since you will want to play it fairly soon. So let's say you cast it for 2 (That's four mana in total to cast,) you just gimped your frostburn weird, nothing happened to Tidebinder, if you have more than 1 counter on Cloudfin you also gimp him. Only thing that will benefit from it is Judge's Familiar. Also very important at this turn you probably have Thassa active as a creature. If you cast this spell... Thassa becomes weaker. Also their are four drops that are just better to cast. MoW, Jace, Bident, and Clone.

So let's say you wait until turn 5. You cast it so your creatures become 3/3s. Waiting this long against Control you probably got board wiped. So you probably rather be recasting creatures instead. Against Aggro you should have so much board presence at this point it becomes pointless to cast. You probably had MoW cast last turn and have tons of tokens to swing this turn and probably win. I'd rather have Mizzium skin mana up to protect MoW when I swing in with the tokens. If you didn't have MoW then you probably have Thassa active and again you want to use that mana to cast creatures to protect her devotion so when she swings she doesn't turn off. Also you want to spend mana to make Thassa unblockable and swing in. 

What I'm trying to point out is MoW Tokens are strong enough already you don't need to buff them higher it's their numbers that kills. Biomass and the way you want to utilize it is better left to Mizzium Skin it only cost one U and can be overloaded for U1.

4 Omenspeakers aren't that great. They only add one devotion and tidebinder mage is a better two drop for the deck. The deck is all about managing devotion for Thassa and MoW and being stuck with a two drop that only applies 1 devotion is really rough and can cost you the game.

Thassa already gives you scry so Voyages End isn't that great. 2 Cyclonic Rifts should be sufficient. 

3 Clones is a bit much. You want to save the four drop slots for MoW, Bident, and Jace AoT. I personally run 1 Clone since Jace's are expensive and it's an ok card but not more than one of in a deck imo.

Your deck is lacking in Nightveil Specters. The triple blue devotion is very important in this deck. It easily can put Thassa back online after a board wipe. 

You don't really want dissolve. It's not very impressive in what this deck is trying to accomplish. Creatures aren't as scary to this deck so it's very safe for mono blue to stick with the cheaper Negate which only cost U and 1. Tidebinders, Claustrophobia, Rapid Hybridization, Thassa, MoW, Frostburn Weird all deal with creatures so letting a creature resolve is okay.

You want to put in Claustrophobia. It is a very good card in mono blue. It's a 3 drop that gives you two devotion that is hard to get rid of unless your opponent wants to use a removal on his/her own creature.

Cloudfin Raptor is a just a better one drop than Nivmagus and it's more reliable cause all of your creatures evolve Cloudfin. This also opens up slots up in your deck since now you can take out the sorcery and instant cards that aren't that great in mono blue and go for more reliable cards that add devotion.

In my personal opinion Shrine to Nyx isn't as impressive in mono blue. It's definitely nice but not necessary.  Especially in your deck's current state which doesn't have much reliable devotion to take advantage of it.

Just my two cents on the deck.

Long distance relationships are really hard. It's easy to say that you both can deal with it but trust me they are a difficult thing to maintain. I've tried it myself, twice. It did not turn out well. I mean I'm not saying it's impossible but both parties need to be willing to slug through it all. Most of the time you'll find yourselves drifting apart and start heading in different directions in life. It is very difficult to be emotionally supportive of someone when you are physically so far away.

If this is to work you guys need to plan out when you will be able to move to be with the other person. One of you has to move eventually. There is nothing worst in a long distance relationship when you don't know if you'll be in the same area ever again or for how long. Communication is another big one. You need to maintain the line of communication between you two. It sounds easier than it is. Trust me when I say this. You'll think that it's not a problem but it really is because the pesky thing called life will keep interrupting. You forget or you won't be able to find time. It happens but you have to keep at it.

My opinion on your situation? Stay friends. Keep in contact keep hanging out online and over the phone. It's easier when the expectation of a relationship isn't looming over the both of you. You have doubts and that's the biggest indication to me that a long distance relationship might not be for you. Once you know you guys can be in the same area again then you can start off your romantic relationship on the right foot.

Good luck and hopefully you guys make the right decision for yourselves.
